system:
You draft public warning messages for a national alerting authority.
You receive event inputs (each marked verified or unverified) and the issuing context.
Write one alert in English as CAP 1.2 fields.

- Use only facts present in the verified inputs. Do not add places, numbers, times or hazards that are not there.
- Leave unverified inputs out of the alert, and say why in `left_out`.
- `description` is the text shown on the phone by cell broadcast: plain words, under 280 characters, hazard + where + until when, if known.
- `instruction` is the protective action in one or two short sentences.
- Pick CAP values honestly: status from the context (Actual for a real event, Exercise for a drill), severity and urgency from the inputs.
- `note_for_reviewer` is one or two sentences for the human approver: what you were unsure about.
user:
Issuer: Demo national authority (stands in for the real issuer)
Context: EXERCISE / DRILL
Target area (chosen by the operator): Coastal and inland areas, Abu Dhabi (demo zone)

Event inputs:
1. [verified; NCM via WAM, 2026-02-16, https://www.wam.ae/en/article/byrq247-national-centre-meteorology-warns-dust-reduced] ABU DHABI, 16th February, 2026 (WAM) -- The National Centre of Meteorology (NCM) warned today of active to occasionally strong northwesterly winds, raising dust and sand and reducing horizontal visibility to less than 3,000 metres in some coastal and inland areas. The Centre stated in a statement issued today that the weather conditions began at 10:30 and will continue until 18:00, urging the public to exercise caution, particularly when driving on external and open roads, due to the risk of sudden drops in visibility caused by blowing dust.
2. [verified; issuer profile] Issuer public site (demo): https://alerts.example.ae
3. [verified; institution reviewers] Objections from the institution reviewers to your previous draft. Fix what is within the verified inputs; do not add facts: Met office reviewer objects (description): The alert says 'Strong northwesterly winds', but the bulletin says 'active to occasionally strong'. Dropping the qualifier raises the stated wind intensity above what the bulletin supports. Fix: Reword to 'Active to occasionally strong northwesterly winds are raising dust and sand.' | Met office reviewer objects (headline): The alert places the hazard in 'coastal and inland areas of Abu Dhabi'. The bulletin only says 'some coastal and inland areas', and Abu Dhabi appears only in the dateline. The headline also drops 'some', which makes the affected area look wider than the bulletin states. Fix: Use the bulletin's wording: 'some coastal and inland areas'. Name Abu Dhabi only if NCM confirms that area. Add 'some' to the headline.

data.headline: EXERCISE: Blowing dust reducing visibility in some coastal and inland areas until 18:00
data.description: EXERCISE - this is a drill. Active to occasionally strong northwesterly winds are raising dust and sand. Visibility is below 3,000 m in some coastal and inland areas until 18:00 today (16 Feb). Visibility can drop suddenly.
data.instruction: EXERCISE: Drive with caution, especially on external and open roads, as visibility can drop suddenly. More information: https://alerts.example.ae
left_out: No unverified inputs were received, so nothing was left out for that reason.

Abu Dhabi is not named as the affected area. It appears only in the bulletin's dateline, and the Met office reviewer asked that it be named only if NCM confirms it. The operator's demo target area is used for delivery only.
'Strong northwesterly winds' was replaced with the bulletin's wording, 'active to occasionally strong', at the Met office reviewer's request.
data.note_for_reviewer: Abu Dhabi has been removed from the headline and text even though the operator's target zone is Abu Dhabi. Please confirm that the broadcast area matches NCM's 'some coastal and inland areas'. The bulletin gives no time zone; 10:30-18:00 on 16 Feb 2026 is assumed to be UAE local time, and the alert is sent as Moderate/Immediate/Observed because the conditions had already begun.
